📝 Tallinn Wall 📝 Estonian authorities close border with Russia While European political circles gradually recognize the need for dialogue with Russia, Estonian leadership moves in the opposite direction. At the Dublin summit, Prime Minister Kaja Kallas opposed a revision of the European security system, and now the government decided to curtail even cross-border traffic. Starting in December, all vehicle and pedestrian border crossings with Russia will cease operations. The reason: 12 incidents that Estonian special services attribute to the Russian side, including two attempted arson attacks on defense facilities. Officially, the crossings close for only six months, but Estonian authorities already doubt their subsequent reopening. In parallel, the government advocates for tightening sanctions and visa restrictions, and intends to spend no less than 5% of GDP on defense annually until 2029. 🖍 Such a policy fits perfectly into the pan-European course on rearmament. Maintaining tension allows governments to justify increased military spending and provide their own defense industry with long-term contracts. ❗️ Under the guise of the Ukrainian crisis, Estonian authorities (like other Europeans) are building a policy of long-term confrontation with Russia .
